name: Early-onset Idiopathic Chronic Pancreatitis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for Chronic Pancreatitis

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of pancreatitis without identifiable cause
Imaging findings consistent with chronic pancreatitis (e.g., pancreatic ductal irregularities, calcifications)
Evidence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency (e.g., steatorrhea, malabsorption)
Exclusion of known causes such as genetic mutations, alcohol use, or obstructive etiologies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent pancreatitis episodes plus imaging evidence of chronic pancreatitis and exclusion of known causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended to exclude hereditary pancreatitis; diagnosis is clinical and radiological after ruling out secondary causes.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic episodic abdominal pain due to pancreatic inflammation
Visible on imaging, highly suggestive of chronic pancreatitis

common.notes: Persistent or intermittent pain in the upper abdomen

common.symptomName: Steatorrhea due to exocrine pancreatic insufficiency
searchTerms: fatty stools from pancreas enzyme deficiency
oily diarrhea due to poor digestion

common.notes: Unintentional weight loss common in advanced disease
searchTerms: weight loss from poor nutrient absorption

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting during acute exacerbations
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting during pancreas attacks

occasional.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to endocrine pancreatic insufficiency
occasional.notes: Develops in later stages due to islet cell damage
searchTerms: high blood sugar due to pancreas failure

occasional.notes: Occasionally caused by inflammation or fibrosis compressing bile ducts
searchTerms: jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile

occasional.notes: Secondary to chronic disease and nutrient deficiencies
searchTerms: weakness due to lack of nutrients

occasional.notes: Fluid collections may develop as a complication

rare.notes: Rare vascular complication secondary to inflammation
Rare leakage of pancreatic fluid into peritoneal cavity
Long-term risk in chronic pancreatitis patients

laboratory: Elevated serum amylase and lipase during acute episodes
Fecal elastase deficiency indicating exocrine insufficiency
Hyperglycemia in cases with endocrine insufficiency
imaging: Pancreatic ductal irregularities and strictures on MRCP or ERCP
Pancreatic calcifications on abdominal CT or X-ray
Atrophic pancreas with fibrosis on imaging
genetic: Absence of mutations in PRSS1, SPINK1, CFTR genes (to exclude hereditary pancreatitis)
other: Pancreatic function tests showing decreased enzyme output
Histopathology (rarely performed) showing fibrosis and acinar cell loss

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of pathogenic mutations in PRSS1 or SPINK1 genes
Earlier onset with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Associated liver disease or alcohol-related complications

redFlags: Sudden worsening of abdominal pain with signs of systemic inflammation
Rapid onset of diabetes mellitus in a young patient with pancreatitis
references: Orphanet: Early-onset idiopathic chronic pancreatitis - ORPHA:700136
Whitcomb DC. Chronic pancreatitis: new genetic developments. Gastroenterology. 2013.
